verdicts.opus: C and D were both grounded in the recorded Prism responses and both flagged the 7-paper intersection limit. A and B relied on memory, and B's citations did not match its effect sizes. C edged D by covering more facets: the full trend with peak and CAGR, the news thirds, and a traced cause-specific effect chart. D was slightly cleaner on accuracy but charted and exported only research volume.
verdicts.gpt: A best supports a decision: it pairs traceable mortality effect estimates with clear limits on what the selected corpus can establish, and it makes the policy implication conditional on observational evidence. B includes more material but introduces an unresolved, directionally inconsistent news trend and an unsupported study window; C and D rely on unverified memory estimates and conflicting reference details.
